gaps: Morphology and diagnosis were not assessed in this batch.
The study's foraging and age-class analyses do not assess the species' full reproductive, developmental or lifespan profile.

claims.text: In a 2009–2010 field study, 608 fruit-foraging focal follows from 49 habituated wild Cebus capucinus in three groups at Pacuare Nature Reserve were used in the return-rate analysis. Adults had higher return rates than younger age classes for fruits ranked difficult to acquire; the paper reports no significant age-class differences for easy-to-acquire fruits. These are results from this study sample and its ordinal food-difficulty categories, not a species-wide diet estimate.
claims.locator: Methods, Study groups, Data collection and Data analyses; Results, Return rates for difficult-, medium-, and easy-to-acquire fruits (608 follows and age-class contrasts); Abstract (adult versus younger age classes).
claims.placeTimeScope: Pacuare Nature Reserve, Limón Province, Costa Rica (10°10′N, 83°14′W); observations collected October 2009–August 2010 from three groups in the reserve's southern portion. The 49 individuals were distributed across the author's defined age classes; the article's main results report 608 analyzed fruit-foraging focal follows.
claims.lifeStatus: Habituated, wild, free-ranging capuchins; no captive or domesticated animals in this claim.

gaps: The study concerns fruit-foraging return rates at one reserve and does not characterize the full diet, seasonal ecology, or species-wide interaction network.
Food difficulty was assigned using ordinal strength and skill categories, and the authors note limitations in these measures and in rank control.
No species phylogeny, comparative evolutionary analysis or divergence estimate was assessed.

claims.text: The paper documents three study groups of Cebus capucinus in the southern portion of Pacuare Nature Reserve, Limón Province, Costa Rica; the field study is a local occurrence record and does not establish the species' range.
claims.locator: Methods, Study site and permits; Study groups; Data collection.
claims.placeTimeScope: Pacuare Nature Reserve, Limón Province, Costa Rica (reported at 10°10′N, 83°14′W); groups identified and habituated 2005–2009; foraging observations October 2009–August 2010.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild, habituated study groups; no occurrence data for captive animals or other locations included.

gaps: One-site evidence does not define the geographic range, native versus introduced limits, range-wide sampling completeness or other occurrence areas.
No fossil search or fossil occurrence evidence was assessed.
No current conservation assessment, status, trend or population-risk analysis was assessed.

reasons: Evidence is limited to local fruit-foraging and occurrence observations; five facets are not assessed and ecology/distribution remain partial.
The 49-animal, three-group sample from one reserve cannot represent the species-wide diet or range.
No independent expert review has been completed.
